significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that a distinct internal adjustment signal in scientific tabular foundation models tracks the backdoor-adjusted effect rather than raw association, "cross[es] zero at the correct confounding strength," and causally shifts predictions toward the do-calculus answer; this combines a form-(iii) predictive coupling with a form-(ii) causal claim. It would establish both a phenomenon—the selective "confounder-in-vs-out sign-flip"—and a mechanism—the decodable and steerable adjustment signal—while fixing expected internal behavior across a continuum of confounding strengths, which is more constraining than the topic-median probe-and-steer hypothesis. Hollmann et al.'s Nature 2025 TabPFN work grounds these models as predictive systems trained on synthetic data priors, while CLadder (Jin et al., NeurIPS 2023) documents the practical separation between causal reasoning and ordinary prediction; a negative result here would therefore informatively reject the specific internal-adjustment account for the tested model class, though not for foundation models generally. Verified-true and verified-false outcomes are distinguishable, and the topic-substitution check passes: deleting the claimed sign-crossing, confounder-specific response, and causal adjustment signal leaves only the generic scientific-representation topic, which would not merit this score.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "Adjustment-Beyond-Observational Index," the "Confounder-In-vs-Out Flip Asymmetry," the dose-response sign-crossing, and the recovered "adjustment direction," collectively framed as an "evaluation standard for causal competence." The benchmark and probe can be ex ante handles because they can screen or gate a tabular model before it is trusted for causal-effect use, whereas steering the direction on observed cases is principally an intervention and diagnostic within the research workflow. After re-extraction on another model, the claim predicts the adjustment-versus-association relationship only for models that possess the hypothesized mechanism; it does not give a universal numerical curve or guarantee that a new architecture will contain the same signal, so much of what transfers is the audit procedure rather than a model-independent law. Its asserted scope spans tabular/scientific foundation models and synthetic, drug-outcome, and omics tasks, with plausible uptake by model auditors and deployment gatekeepers; the topic-substitution check passes because the generic topic alone supplies none of these ex-ante handles.
